the learning algorithm combines Hebbian learning with a delayed reinforcement procedure, that perfect generalization is obtained for a non-zero initial overlap between teacher and student weight vectors, and that the generalization error decreases as a power law of the number of learning examples.

(i) learning with incomplete information can be realized in a committee machine; (ii) perfect generalization is obtained for sufficiently strong Hebbian learning; and (iii) the generalization error decays as a power law with an exponent depending on the strength of Hebbean learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the learning of a student with incomplete information about a teacher can result in perfect generalization.
the problem of learning a teacher’s rule in a student-teacher setup, when the student has incomplete information.
the question of how to learn with incomplete information in an unsupervised setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the learning algorithm studied here is capable of perfect generalization in a wide range of parameter regimes, including cases with incomplete information.
the committee machine is able to learn with incomplete information, and to do so with an optimal resolution of complexity mismatches, provided the learning parameter is above the bifurcation point.

the system exhibits a phase transition from perfect generalization (for λ > λc) to a state of imperfect generalization (for the case of λ < λc), which can be interpreted as a transition to a state of chaos.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the learning algorithm we propose can be used to emulate a complex teacher rule with a less complex student, and to resolve a complexity mismatch between the two.

a learning algorithm with incomplete information can be successful if it combines unsupervised learning with a reinforcement step, and that it can optimally resolve cases of a complexity-mismatch between student and teacher.

learning in the committee machine is possible in the presence of incomplete information, and that the learning process is characterized by an interplay between the learning parameter and the complexity mismatch.

the learning algorithm is able to deal with a complexity mismatch between teacher and student.
learning with incomplete information, i.e. with only partial access to the training examples, can lead to a better generalization performance than learning from complete information.
